criteria: Does the shot contain exactly ONE main idea/focal point?
Is counterchange applied (light over dark, dark over light)?
Are all extreme poses perfectly readable in black silhouette?
Are anticipation, action, and aftermath clearly defined?
Does the camera stay on the established side of the 180-degree line?
Are moving holds utilized instead of dead/frozen holds?
Is twinning avoided in extreme poses?
Do locomotion cycles include Contact, Down, Passing, and Up beats?
Do wrists/nose/hips travel on arcs rather than straight lines?
Do eyes/eyelids lead head turns by 2-4 frames?
Does follow-through settle 4-8 frames after the root stops?
Is center of gravity over the planted foot before a leg lifts?
Is there 12-24 frames of breathing room after major actions?
Do talking scenes include physical action that carries subtext?
Is each character extreme built on a clear asymmetrical line of action?
Is camera movement motivated by character or story reveal?
Is look-space provided in the direction the character is looking?
Do compositional lines return the eye to the focal point?
Do reverse shots reverse eyelines correctly?
Is physical cause shown before effect across cuts?
Is screen direction preserved for exiting/entering objects?
Does each shot answer what is going on and why we should care?
Do high-tension rapid cuts have resting periods afterward?
Do craft mechanics stay below the threshold of awareness?
Is the Down/recoil breakdown present so motion has weight?
